metadata.title: Breast Pathology Knowledge Base for RAG
sources: Libre Pathology - Breast, IDC, ILC, DCIS, Mucinous, Tubular, Medullary, Grading, Staging, HER2, ER
metadata.purpose: Structured knowledge base for breast pathology RAG system in WSI VQA

aliases: Invasive carcinoma of no special type
invasive_ductal_carcinoma_NST.definition: The most common form of invasive breast cancer, arising from terminal duct-lobular units. Diagnosed by exclusion of special subtypes. Alternatively termed invasive carcinoma of No Specific/Special Type (NST).
invasive_ductal_carcinoma_NST.gross_features: White, firm stellate lesion with irregular borders. Hard consistency due to desmoplastic stromal reaction.

histological_features.architecture: Highly variable. Atypical cells forming ducts, sheets, cords, or nests with variable mitotic activity and necrosis. Infiltrative pattern with small glands of variable size within desmoplastic stroma. Glands lined by a single layer of cells (loss of myoepithelial layer).
histological_features.cytology: Atypical cells typically exceed 2x RBC diameter, though may appear bland in well-differentiated variants. Nucleoli commonly present. Variable nuclear pleomorphism.
histological_features.key_diagnostic_finding: Atypical nucleus adjacent to adipocytes (indicating invasion). Absence of myoepithelial cells confirmed by IHC (p63 negative, SMMS negative).
histological_features.invasion_pattern: Infiltrative small glands of variable size within desmoplastic stroma

immunohistochemistry.E_cadherin: Strong membranous positivity (distinguishes from ILC); note: up to 3-5% may be negative, especially higher grade tumors

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: DCIS is confined within basement membrane; IDC shows invasion into stroma. IHC for myoepithelial markers (p63, SMA, calponin) helps distinguish.
ILC shows single-file infiltration, E-cadherin negative. IDC forms glands/sheets, E-cadherin positive.
Benign; retains myoepithelial cells on IHC
Special type with >90% well-formed angulated tubules, excellent prognosis

invasive_ductal_carcinoma_NST.prognosis: Variable, dependent on stage, grade, and molecular subtype. Ranges from good (low grade, small, node-negative) to poor (high grade, node-positive, triple-negative).

invasive_lobular_carcinoma.frequency: 10-15% of invasive breast cancers (second most common)
invasive_lobular_carcinoma.definition: Second most common form of invasive breast cancer, characterized by discohesive cells infiltrating in single-file patterns with loss of E-cadherin expression.
invasive_lobular_carcinoma.gross_features: Often clinically occult; may not form a discrete mass. Frequently multifocal and bilateral. Diffuse firmness rather than a defined lump.

histological_features.classic_pattern: Single-file cell arrangement (Indian file pattern). Discohesive cells. No gland formation. Absence of desmoplastic reaction - surrounding stroma appears benign and undisturbed. Low-grade nuclear characteristics typically. Targetoid pattern: tumor cells concentrically arranged around normal ducts.
histological_features.cytology: Small, uniform cells with eccentric nuclei. Signet ring cell morphology may occur. Intracytoplasmic lumina may be present.

variants.classic: Low nuclear grade, single-file pattern, small uniform cells without significant nuclear size variation
variants.pleomorphic: Significant nuclear atypia, larger cells, higher grade, may show apocrine features. More aggressive behavior.
variants.solid: Sheets of discohesive cells without single-file pattern
variants.alveolar: Cells arranged in small round clusters of approximately 20 cells
variants.tubulolobular: Small tubules admixed with single-file lobular pattern
variants.histiocytoid: Cells resemble histiocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm

immunohistochemistry.E_cadherin: NEGATIVE (defining feature, loss due to CDH1 mutation/inactivation)

invasive_lobular_carcinoma.genetic_associations: May be associated with CDH1 mutation, linked to hereditary diffuse gastric cancer syndrome.

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: IDC forms glands/sheets, E-cadherin positive. ILC shows single-file, E-cadherin negative.
LCIS is non-invasive, confined to lobules. ILC invades stroma.
May mimic ILC; E-cadherin status helps distinguish.
Melanoma markers (S100, HMB-45, Melan-A) positive; cytokeratins negative.

invasive_lobular_carcinoma.prognosis: Generally similar stage-for-stage to IDC but differs in metastatic pattern (more frequent metastasis to peritoneum, GI tract, ovaries, meninges).

ductal_carcinoma_in_situ.frequency: 20-25% of all breast cancers detected by screening
ductal_carcinoma_in_situ.definition: Non-invasive breast carcinoma confined within the ductal basement membrane. Diagnosed through nuclear abnormalities and/or architectural changes.

histological_features.nuclear_features: Nuclear enlargement at least 2-3x size of RBC. Nuclear pleomorphism. Mitoses variably present.
histological_features.architectural_features: Equal spacing of cells ('cookie cutter' look). Cells align along lumens forming 'Roman bridges'. Architecture varies by subtype.

architectural_subtypes.comedo: Central necrosis within ducts filled with high-grade cells. Often associated with calcifications. High-grade nuclei with central luminal necrosis ('comedo' = comedone-like). Most aggressive pattern.
architectural_subtypes.cribriform: Honeycomb-like appearance with circular holes, 'cookie cutter' or 'punched-out' appearance. Regular, round secondary lumina within cell masses. Often low to intermediate grade.
architectural_subtypes.solid: Sheet of cells fills the duct with no intercellular spaces. May be associated with comedonecrosis.
architectural_subtypes.micropapillary: Small papillae WITHOUT fibrovascular cores. Characteristic 'drum stick' shape projecting into lumen. No supporting stromal axis.
architectural_subtypes.papillary: Papillae WITH fibrovascular cores LACKING myoepithelial layers, lined by atypical cells. Distinguished from benign papilloma by absence of myoepithelial cells.

ductal_carcinoma_in_situ.distinction_from_ADH: Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia (ADH) diagnosed if <2 membrane-bound spaces AND <2 mm extent (3 mm for papillary lesions). Both receive excision, but DCIS requires radiation; ADH does not.

immunohistochemistry.myoepithelial_layer: PRESENT (distinguishes from invasive carcinoma). Confirmed by CK5/6, SMA, p63, calponin.

ductal_carcinoma_in_situ.key_diagnostic_principle: Architecture is more important than cytologic features in the diagnosis of malignancy in the breast; low-grade tumors have distorted architecture but normal/near-normal cytology.

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: Size <2mm and <2 involved spaces = ADH rather than DCIS
LCIS shows discohesive cells filling lobules, E-cadherin negative. DCIS fills ducts with cohesive cells, E-cadherin positive.
DCIS retains myoepithelial layer; invasive carcinoma does not.
UDH shows streaming pattern with slit-like spaces, heterogeneous cell population. DCIS shows monotonous cell population with architectural abnormalities.

mucinous_carcinoma.definition: Invasive breast carcinoma characterized by abundant extracellular mucin production. Mucinous component must comprise >90% of the tumor for pure mucinous diagnosis.
mucinous_carcinoma.gross_features: Pale, glistening, jelly-like appearance. Typically well-circumscribed.

histological_features.architecture: Malignant mucin-producing glands with small clusters of cells floating in mucin pools. Glands typically display irregular edges. Vessels may be present within mucin pools.
histological_features.cytology: Low to intermediate nuclear grade. Cells appear to float within abundant mucinous material.
histological_features.key_criteria: Mucinous component must be >90% for pure mucinous diagnosis

subtypes.mucinous_A_paucicellular: Greater mucin component, fewer tumor cells within mucin lakes
subtypes.mucinous_B_hypercellular: Less mucin, more cellular, with neuroendocrine differentiation and argyrophilia

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: Mucin appears homogenous, lacks vascularization, and has regular borders
Any NST component >10% = mixed rather than pure mucinous; worse prognosis
Benign, mucin-filled cysts without malignant epithelium

mucinous_carcinoma.prognosis: Good prognosis (better than IDC-NST). Pure mucinous has better prognosis than mixed. Admixture with NST component worsens prognosis. Typically affects older women.
mucinous_carcinoma.clinical_context: Core biopsy showing any mucinous change warrants excision to exclude mucinous carcinoma.

medullary_carcinoma.frequency: Uncommon subtype, <5% of invasive breast cancers. More frequent in BRCA1 mutation carriers.
medullary_carcinoma.definition: Poorly differentiated but well-circumscribed invasive carcinoma with syncytial growth, prominent lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, and pushing borders. All five diagnostic criteria must be met.
diagnostic_criteria_all_required: Syncytial growth pattern (clumps of cells with poorly defined cell borders, >75% of tumor)
Lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate (prominent, within and around tumor)
High nuclear grade (as per Nottingham grading system)

histological_features.architecture: Syncytial sheets of large pleomorphic cells. Well-circumscribed with pushing margins. Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate throughout. No glandular/tubular differentiation.
histological_features.cytology: High nuclear grade. Large cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Poorly defined cell borders (syncytial appearance). High mitotic rate.

immunohistochemistry.note: Characteristically triple-negative. Know when to discuss BRCA mutations, triple negativity and the 'basal-like molecular phenotype' in basaloid lesions.

medullary_carcinoma.genetic_associations: May be associated with BRCA1 mutation. More frequent in younger patients.

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: Lacks one or more of the five strict criteria. Called 'atypical medullary carcinoma' or 'IDC with medullary features'.
Lymphoma is LCA/CD45 positive, cytokeratin negative. Medullary carcinoma is cytokeratin positive.

medullary_carcinoma.prognosis: Better prognosis than IDC-NST despite high grade appearance. Favorable outcomes attributed to immune infiltrate and circumscription.

tubular_carcinoma.definition: Well-differentiated invasive breast carcinoma composed of well-formed angulated tubules lacking myoepithelial cells. May look like benign breast tissue at initial examination.
diagnostic_criteria: Well-formed tubules with characteristic angled ducts described as 'prows'
Absence of myoepithelial cells (diagnostic, confirmed by IHC)
Greater than 70% of tumor cells must be adjacent to luminal spaces
Open luminal spaces with single layer of cells

histological_features.architecture: Well-formed angulated tubules with pointed/angular contours ('prows'). Haphazard arrangement within stroma. Single layer of cuboidal to columnar epithelium. Open lumina.
histological_features.cytology: Minimal cytologic atypia. Low nuclear grade. Low mitotic rate. Apocrine snouts at luminal surface.

immunohistochemistry.HER2: Negative (positivity should prompt consideration of another diagnosis)

tubular_carcinoma.associated_findings: Rosen triad: concurrent occurrence with LCIS and columnar cell lesions.

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_features: Benign; retains myoepithelial cells. Lobulocentric architecture.
Round (not angulated) glands, S100 positive, ER negative.
Benign; retains myoepithelial layer. Central fibroelastic core.

tubular_carcinoma.prognosis: Excellent prognosis, significantly better than IDC-NST. Classically seen in post-menopausal women. Very low recurrence rate.

nottingham_grading_system.purpose: Standard histologic grading system for invasive breast carcinomas. Useful prognosticator performed routinely on all invasive breast cancers.

tubule_formation.description: Percentage of tumor area showing definite tubule or gland formation

nuclear_pleomorphism.description: Degree of variation in nuclear size, shape, and chromatin pattern
nuclear_pleomorphism.score_1: Small, regular nuclei (1.5-2x RBC diameter). Uniform chromatin. Minimal variation.
nuclear_pleomorphism.score_2: Moderate variation in nuclear size and shape. Nuclei 2-2.5x RBC diameter.
nuclear_pleomorphism.score_3: Marked variation in nuclear size and shape (>2.5x RBC diameter). Prominent nucleoli. Vesicular chromatin.

mitotic_count.description: Number of mitoses per 10 high-power fields (HPF). Field area must be specified (standard: 0.152 mm2 per HPF at 40x with field diameter of 0.44mm; some scopes use 1.52 mm2 total for 10 HPF).
mitotic_count.note: Modern microscopes typically have 0.2376 mm2 field diameter at 40x, requiring approximately 6-7 fields for proper sampling. Counts are field-area dependent.

primary_tumor_T.Tis: Carcinoma in situ (DCIS); Paget disease without associated tumor
primary_tumor_T.T1a: >1 mm but <=5 mm (round any measurement 1.0-1.9 mm to 2 mm)
primary_tumor_T.T4: Any size with direct extension to chest wall and/or skin
primary_tumor_T.T4a: Extension to chest wall (not including pectoralis muscle)
primary_tumor_T.T4b: Ulceration, ipsilateral satellite skin nodules, or skin edema (including peau d'orange)

regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN0_i_plus: Isolated tumor cells <=0.2 mm and <200 cells
regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN1mi: Micrometastasis >0.2 mm and/or >200 cells but <=2 mm
regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN1: 1-3 axillary lymph nodes positive and/or internal mammary nodes with micrometastasis
regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN1a: 1-3 positive axillary nodes, at least one >2 mm
regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN1b: Internal mammary nodes with micrometastasis by sentinel node biopsy
regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN2: 4-9 positive axillary nodes or clinically detected internal mammary nodes
regional_lymph_nodes_N.pN3: >=10 positive axillary nodes, or infraclavicular nodes, or supraclavicular nodes

distant_metastasis_M.cM0_i_plus: No clinical/radiographic evidence of metastasis but molecularly/microscopically detected tumor cells <=0.2 mm in blood, bone marrow, or non-regional nodes

stage_groupings.stage_IIA: T0-T1 N1 M0 or T2 N0 M0
stage_groupings.stage_IIB: T2 N1 M0 or T3 N0 M0
stage_groupings.stage_IIIA: T0-T2 N2 M0 or T3 N1-N2 M0

estrogen_receptor_ER.purpose: Predictive biomarker for endocrine therapy response. Class II IHC test used directly for treatment decisions.

allred_score.description: Proportion Score (PS, 0-5) + Intensity Score (IS, 0-3) = Total Score (0 or 2-8)

interpretation.3-8: Positive (higher score = greater benefit from endocrine therapy)

percentage_method.positive: >=1% of tumor nuclei staining (per ASCO/CAP 2010 guidelines)
percentage_method.ER_low_positive: 1-10% staining (uncertain clinical benefit; consider repeat testing)

H_score.formula: (1 x % weakly staining) + (2 x % moderately staining) + (3 x % strongly staining)

estrogen_receptor_ER.clinical_significance: About 75% of invasive breast cancers are ER-positive. ER-positive tumors benefit from endocrine therapy (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors).

progesterone_receptor_PR.purpose: Predictive and prognostic biomarker. ER+/PR+ tumors have better prognosis and response to endocrine therapy than ER+/PR- tumors.
progesterone_receptor_PR.scoring: Same systems as ER (Allred, percentage, H-score)
progesterone_receptor_PR.clinical_significance: ER-/PR+ tumors are rare (<1%) and should prompt retesting. PR loss in ER+ tumors may indicate more aggressive biology.

HER2.purpose: Predictive biomarker for HER2-targeted therapy (trastuzumab/Herceptin, pertuzumab, T-DM1, T-DXd). Prognostic marker.

score_0.staining: No staining or barely perceptible incomplete membrane staining in <=10% of invasive tumor cells

score_1_plus.staining: Faint/barely perceptible incomplete membrane staining in >10% of invasive tumor cells
score_1_plus.action: No traditional HER2-targeted therapy. May be eligible for T-DXd (HER2-low targeting).

score_2_plus.staining: Weak to moderate complete membrane staining in >10% of cells OR intense complete membrane staining in <=10% of cells
score_2_plus.action: Requires reflex testing with ISH (FISH or SISH)

score_3_plus.staining: Intense complete circumferential membrane staining in >10% of invasive tumor cells

ISH_FISH_criteria.positive: HER2/CEP17 ratio >=2.0 OR HER2 gene copy number >=6.0 copies per cell
ISH_FISH_criteria.equivocal: HER2/CEP17 ratio <2.0 AND HER2 copy number 4.0-6.0 copies per cell
ISH_FISH_criteria.negative: HER2/CEP17 ratio <2.0 AND HER2 copy number <4.0 copies per cell

HER2_low.clinical_relevance: Eligible for antibody-drug conjugates like trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)

HER2.preanalytical_requirements: Cold ischemia time <1 hour recommended (ASCO/CAP guidelines) to preserve specimen integrity.
HER2.clinical_significance: ~15-20% of breast cancers are HER2-positive. HER2 positivity associated with worse prognosis without targeted therapy but good response to HER2-targeted agents.

Ki67.purpose: Proliferation marker used to distinguish Luminal A from Luminal B molecular subtypes

interpretation.low: <14% (some guidelines use <20%): Suggests Luminal A if ER+/HER2-

Ki67.limitations: Lacks standardized quantification methodology. Inter-observer variability is significant.

myoepithelial_cell_principle.description: The key to breast pathology is the myoepithelial cell. Normal breast glands have two cell layers: myoepithelial (outer/basal) and luminal/secretory (inner).

diagnostic_application.present: Benign process or in situ carcinoma (DCIS/LCIS)

ductal_vs_lobular_distinction.ductal_features: Streaming pattern, peripheral slit-like spaces, fibrovascular cores, cohesive cells, E-cadherin positive
ductal_vs_lobular_distinction.lobular_features: Single cells/single file, discohesive appearance, no gland formation, E-cadherin negative

calcification_patterns.calcium_phosphate: Purple globs with concentric rings on H&E. May be associated with malignancy (especially in DCIS).
calcification_patterns.calcium_oxalate: Visible with polarized light. NOT associated with malignancy. Birefringent crystals.
calcification_patterns.diagnostic_significance: Microcalcifications often prompt biopsy. Lesions may be ~100 micrometers in diameter, requiring extensive sectioning (up to 10 levels for calcification-targeted biopsies).

morphological_patterns.architectural_importance: Architecture is more important than cytologic features in the diagnosis of malignancy in the breast. Low-grade tumors have distorted architecture but normal/near-normal cytology.

benign_vs_malignant.features: Inflammation resembling inflammatory breast cancer; responds to antibiotics. Neutrophilic infiltrate. No malignant cells.
Traumatic hardening mimicking malignancy on imaging. Foamy macrophages, foreign body giant cells. No malignant epithelium.
Benign biphasic tumor (epithelial + stromal). Well-circumscribed. Retains myoepithelial layer. >2cm typically excised.
Cysts, apocrine metaplasia, fibrosis. Non-proliferative. No increased cancer risk.
Streaming pattern with slit-like spaces, heterogeneous cell population. Distinguished from DCIS by irregular architecture and mixed cell types.
Retains myoepithelial cells (IHC confirmed). Lobulocentric. Distorted but preserved two-cell-layer architecture.
Central fibroelastic core with radiating ducts. Retains myoepithelial layer. Requires imaging correlation.

papillary_lesions.benign_papilloma: Myoepithelial cells PRESENT. Fibrovascular cores arising from duct wall. No/low-grade atypia.
papillary_lesions.papillary_DCIS: Fibrovascular cores arising from tufts (not directly from wall). Myoepithelial cells ABSENT on cores. Monotonous atypical cell population.
papillary_lesions.intracystic_papillary_carcinoma: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma. No myoepithelial cells. Low-grade nuclei in most cases.
papillary_lesions.size_threshold: Atypia extent >3mm favors DCIS over ADH in papillary lesions

spindle_cell_lesions.features: Cytokeratin positive. May show squamous, spindle, or matrix-producing differentiation.
Biphasic (epithelial + stromal). Leaf-like architecture. Stromal overgrowth in malignant variant.
Beta-catenin nuclear positive. Infiltrative borders. No epithelial component.

flat_epithelial_atypia_FEA.description: Columnar cell change with low-grade cytologic atypia. Significant risk marker for subsequent carcinoma.

atypical_ductal_hyperplasia_ADH.description: Shares features with low-grade DCIS but smaller extent (<2mm or <2 spaces). Moderate risk elevation.

lobular_carcinoma_in_situ_LCIS.description: Discohesive cells filling and expanding lobules. E-cadherin negative. Risk marker for bilateral breast cancer.

florid_epithelial_hyperplasia_UDH.description: 3-4+ cell layers above basement membrane. Variable cells. No nuclear atypia. Moderate risk elevation.

core_needle_biopsy.calcifications: Typically 10 levels (lesions ~100 micrometers require extensive sectioning)

lumpectomy_orientation.convention: Short suture = superior, Long suture = lateral
lumpectomy_orientation.margin_assessment: Inked margins evaluated for distance of tumor from resection edge

mastectomy.note: Usually done with sentinel lymph node biopsy as one cannot go back later to do this

epidemiology.incidence: Most common cancer diagnosed in women globally. Approximately 11.7% of new cancer cases in 2020.
epidemiology.lifetime_risk: 1 in 8 women and 1 in 1000 men in the US
epidemiology.age_distribution: 95% of new cases occur in women aged 40 years or older
risk_factors: Family history / genetic mutations (BRCA1/BRCA2: 5-10% of all breast cancer cases)
Early menarche, late first childbirth, nulliparity, late menopause
Histologic precursors (LCIS, proliferative changes with atypia)
